entries.label: EVPN Instance (EVI)
entries.definition: The EVPN instance realising one Ethernet VPN service (a MAC-VRF).

entries.label: Attachment Circuit (AC)
entries.definition: The circuit or interface by which a customer site attaches to a provider-edge router.
entries.example: the AC on PE1 for the ACME headquarters

entries.label: VPN network access
entries.definition: The service's access point at one attachment -- the per-AC network access of the VPN.
entries.example: the VPN network access at the headquarters site

entries.label: bridge domain
entries.definition: The layer-2 bridge domain (customer VLAN) over which the EVPN forwards; one broadcast domain.

entries.label: ingress policer
entries.definition: The ingress committed/excess rate enforced at the attachment.
entries.example: policer at CIR 200 Mbit/s, EIR 50 Mbit/s

entries.label: traffic class
entries.definition: The forwarding class applied to frames on the instance.
entries.example: the traffic class for the real-time queue

entries.label: MAC learning
entries.definition: Learning local customer source-MAC addresses into the MAC-VRF forwarding table; distinct from EVPN MAC mobility.

entries.label: interface MTU
entries.definition: The maximum frame size carried on the interface end to end.

entries.label: Ethernet Segment (ES)
entries.definition: The set of links by which a multi-homed site attaches to more than one provider-edge router, identified by an ESI; a multi-homing construct, not a broadcast domain.
entries.example: the dual-homed site's ESI on PE2 and PE3

entries.label: MAC mobility
entries.definition: The EVPN mechanism handling a customer MAC that relocates between provider-edge routers, using a sequence number; distinct from local MAC learning.
entries.example: a sequence bump when a MAC moves from PE1 to PE2
